240: 			break;
241: 		case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
242: 			ret = pm_cp0_send_msg(LOW_PWR_CORE_CP2_RECOVERY, cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
243: 			break;
244: 		case PM_RTC_DEEPSLEEP_CMD:
245: 			ret = pm_cp0_send_msg(LOW_PWR_CORE_RTC_DEEPSLEEP, cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
246: 			break;
247: 		case PM_GET_PM_DATA_CMD:
248: 			ret = pm_cp0_send_msg(LOW_PWR_CORE_GET_CP_DATA, cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
249: 			break;
250: 		case PM_CTRL_AP_STATE_CMD:
251: 			ret = pm_cp0_send_msg(LOW_PWR_CORE_CTRL_CP2_STATE, cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
252: 			break;
253: 		case PM_ENTER_DEEP_SLEEP_CMD:
254: 			ret = pm_cp0_send_msg(LOW_PWR_CORE_STATE_ENTER_DEEPSLEEP, cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);

258: 			break;
259: 		default:
260: 			break;
261: 	}
262: 	GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
263: 	if(ret != BK_OK)
264: 	{
265: 		BK_LOGD(NULL,"cp0 handle cp1 message error\r\n");
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	//if(pm_debug_mode()&0x2)
269: 	{
270: 		if(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd != PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD)
271: 		{
272: 			BK_LOGV(NULL,"cp0_mb_rx_isr %d %d %d %d %d\r\n",cmd_buf->hdr.cmd,cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3,ret);
273: 		}
274: 	}

327: static void pm_module_bootup_cpu1(pm_power_module_name_e module)
328: {
329: 	uint64_t previous_tick = 0;
330: 	uint64_t current_tick   = 0;
331: 	if(PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF == sys_drv_module_power_state_get(module))
332: 	{
333: 		if(module == PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1)
334: 		{
335: boot_cp1:
336: 			#if CONFIG_PM_AP_POWERDOWN_WHEN_LV
337: 			bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, 0, 0);
338: 			#endif
339:             bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
340: 
341: 			#if defined(RECV_LOG_FROM_MBOX)
342: 			void reset_forward_log_status(void);
343: 			// reset cpu1's log transfer status on cpu0.
344: 			reset_forward_log_status();
345: 			#endif
346: 
347:             start_cpu1_core();
348: 
349: 			previous_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
350: 			current_tick = previous_tick;
351: 			while((current_tick - previous_tick) < (PM_BOOT_CP1_WAITING_TIEM*AON_RTC_MS_TICK_CNT))
352: 			{
353: 				if (bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get()) // wait the cp1 response
354: 				{
355: 					break;
356: 				}
357: 				current_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
358: 			}
359: 
360: 			if(!bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get())
361: 			{
362: 				BK_LOGD(NULL,"cp0 boot cp1[%d] time out, boot cp1 fail!!!\r\n",s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count);
363: 
364: 				/*Reset psram*/
365: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF);
366: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
367: 
368: 				s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count++;
369: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count < PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
370: 				{
371: 					goto boot_cp1;
372: 				}
373: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count == PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
374: 				{
375: 					#if CONFIG_WDT_EN
376: 					bk_wdt_force_reboot();//try 3 times, if fail ,reboot.
377: 					#endif
378: 				}
379: 			}
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: }

428: bk_err_t bk_pm_module_vote_boot_cp1_ctrl(pm_boot_cp1_module_name_e module,pm_power_module_state_e power_state)
429: {
430: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
431: 	GLOBAL_INT_DECLARATION();
432: 
433: 	BK_LOGD(NULL,"boot_cp1 %d %d 0x%x [%d][0x%x]E_1\r\n",module, power_state,s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state,s_pm_cp1_closing,&s_sync_cp1_open_sema);
434: 	if (NULL == s_sync_cp1_open_sema)
435: 	{
436: 		rtos_init_semaphore(&s_sync_cp1_open_sema, 1);
437: 	}
438: 	if(s_pm_cp1_closing)
439: 	{
440: 		GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
441: 		s_pm_cp1_sema_count++;
442: 		GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
443: 		BK_LOGD(NULL,"boot_cp1 get sema[%d][0x%x]\r\n",s_pm_cp1_sema_count,&s_sync_cp1_open_sema);
444: 
445: 		/*add protect:init again when the s_sync_cp1_open_sema free*/
446: 		if (NULL == s_sync_cp1_open_sema)
447: 		{
448: 			rtos_init_semaphore(&s_sync_cp1_open_sema, 1);
449: 		}
450: 		ret = rtos_get_semaphore(&s_sync_cp1_open_sema, PM_OPEN_CP1_TIMEOUT);
451: 
452: 		GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
453: 		s_pm_cp1_sema_count--;
454: 		GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
455: 		if(ret == kTimeoutErr)
456: 		{
457: 			BK_LOGD(NULL,"boot_cp1[%d]0x%llx %d %d %d\r\n",ret,s_pm_cp1_module_recovery_state,bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get(),bk_pm_cp1_recovery_all_state_get(),s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state);

460: 				bk_pm_module_check_cp1_shutdown();
461: 			}
462: 		}
463: 	}
464: 	BK_LOGD(NULL,"boot_cp1 %d %d 0x%x [%d]E_2\r\n",module, power_state,s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state,ret);
465:     if(power_state == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON)//power on
466:     {
467: 		//bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(PM_DEV_ID_CPU1,PM_CPU_FRQ_480M);
468: 		//bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
469: 		GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
470: 		s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state |= 0x1 << (module);
471: 		GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
472: 		pm_module_bootup_cpu1(PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1);
473:     }
474:     else //power down
475:     {
476: 		if(s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state&(0x1 << (module)))
477: 		{
478: 			GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
479: 			s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state &= ~(0x1 << (module));
480: 			GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
481: 			if(0x0 == s_pm_cp1_ctrl_state)
482: 			{
483: 				s_pm_cp1_closing = 1;
484: 				BK_LOGD(NULL,"boot_cp1 %d %d close 0x%llx %d\r\n",module, power_state,s_pm_cp1_module_recovery_state,s_pm_cp1_boot_ready);
485: 				pm_cp0_mailbox_send_data(PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD,0,0,0);
486: 				//pm_module_shutdown_cpu1(PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1);
487: 			}
488: 		}
489:     }
490: 
491:     return BK_OK;
492: }

271: static void pm_cp1_mailbox_rx_isr(int *pm_mb, mb_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_buf)
272: {
273: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
274: 	uint32_t used_count;
275: 
276: 	GLOBAL_INT_DECLARATION();
277: 	GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
278: 	switch(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd) {
279: 		case PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD:
280: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
281: 			{
282: 				s_pm_cp1_pwr_finish = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
283: 			}
284: 			else
285: 			{
286: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
287: 			}
288: 			break;
289: 		case PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD:
290: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
291: 			{
292: 				s_pm_cp1_clk_finish = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
293: 			}
294: 			else
295: 			{
296: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
297: 			}
298: 			break;
299: 		 case PM_SLEEP_CTRL_CMD:
300: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
301: 			{
302: 				s_pm_cp1_sleep_finish = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
303: 			}
304: 			else
305: 			{
306: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
307: 			}
308: 			break;
309: 		 case PM_CPU_FREQ_CTRL_CMD:
310: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
311: 			{
312: 				s_pm_cp1_cpu_freq_finish = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
313: 			}
314: 			else
315: 			{
316: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
317: 			}
318: 			break;
319: 		case PM_CTRL_EXTERNAL_LDO_CMD:
320: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
321: 			{
322: 				s_pm_external_ldo_ctrl = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
323: 			}
324: 			else
325: 			{
326: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
327: 			}
328: 			break;
329: 		case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
330: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == BK_OK)
331: 			{
332: 				s_pm_psram_power_ctrl = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
333: 			}
334: 			else
335: 			{
336: 				ret = BK_FAIL;
337: 			}
338: 			break;
339: 		case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
340: 			used_count = bk_psram_heap_get_used_count();
341: 			pm_cp1_mailbox_send_data(PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,0x1,used_count,0);
342: 			//os_printf("cp1 bk_psram_heap_get_used_count[%d]\r\n", bk_psram_heap_get_used_count());
343: 			break;
344: 		case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
345: 			bk_psram_heap_get_used_state();
346: 			break;
347: 		case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
348: 			stop_cpu1_handle_notifications();
349: 			bk_pm_cp1_ctrl_state_set(PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_INIT);
350: 			break;
351: 		default:
352: 			break;
353: 	}
354: 	GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
355: 
356: 	if(ret != BK_OK)
357: 	{
358: 		os_printf("cp1 resps:cp0 rev msg error\r\n");
359: 	}
360: 	//if(pm_debug_mode()&0x2)
361: 	{
362:       if(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd != PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD)
363:       {
364: 		//os_printf("cp1_mb_rx_isr %d %d %d\r\n",cmd_buf->hdr.cmd,cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
365:       }
366: 	}
367: }

436: static void pm_cp0_mailbox_rx_isr(int *pm_mb, mb_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_buf)
437: {
438: 	bk_err_t ret = BK_OK;
439: 
440: 	GLOBAL_INT_DECLARATION();
441: 	GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE();
442: 	switch(cmd_buf->hdr.cmd) {
443: 		case PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD:
444: 			ret = bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
445: 
446: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_POWER_CTRL_CMD,ret);
447: 
448: 			break;
449: 		case PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD:
450: 			ret = bk_pm_clock_ctrl(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
451: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_CLK_CTRL_CMD,ret);
452: 			break;
453: 		case PM_SLEEP_CTRL_CMD:
454: 			ret = bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
455: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_SLEEP_CTRL_CMD,ret);
456: 			break;
457: 		case PM_CPU_FREQ_CTRL_CMD:
458: 			ret = bk_pm_module_vote_cpu_freq(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
459: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_CPU_FREQ_CTRL_CMD,ret);
460: 			break;
461: 		case PM_CTRL_EXTERNAL_LDO_CMD:
462: 			ret = bk_pm_module_vote_ctrl_external_ldo(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2,cmd_buf->param3);
463: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_CTRL_EXTERNAL_LDO_CMD,ret);
464: 			break;
465: 		case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
466: 			ret = bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
467: 			pm_cp0_mailbox_response(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,ret);
468: 			break;
469: 		case PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD:
470: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == 0x1)
471: 			{
472: 				s_pm_cp1_boot_ready = PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH;
473: 			}
474: 			//if(pm_debug_mode()&0x2)//for temp debug
475: 				os_printf("cpu0 receive the cpu1 boot success event [%d]\r\n",cmd_buf->param1);
476: 			break;
477: 		case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
478: 			if(cmd_buf->param1 == 0x1)
479: 			{
480: 				bk_pm_cp0_psram_malloc_state_set(PM_MAILBOX_COMMUNICATION_FINISH);
481: 				s_pm_cp1_psram_malloc_count = cmd_buf->param2;
482: 			}
483: 			break;
484: 		case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
485: 			bk_pm_cp1_recovery_module_state_ctrl(cmd_buf->param1,cmd_buf->param2);
486: 			//os_printf("pm_cp0_mb_rx_isr CP1_RECOV_CMD\r\n");
487: 			break;
488: 		default:
489: 			break;
490: 	}
491: 	GLOBAL_INT_RESTORE();
492: 	if(ret != BK_OK)
493: 	{
494: 		os_printf("cp0 handle cp1 message error\r\n");
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	//if(pm_debug_mode()&0x2)
498: 	{

556: static void pm_module_bootup_cpu1(pm_power_module_name_e module)
557: {
558: 	uint64_t previous_tick = 0;
559: 	uint64_t current_tick   = 0;
560: 	if(PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF == sys_drv_module_power_state_get(module))
561: 	{
562: 		if(module == PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1)
563: 		{
564: boot_cp1:
565: 			bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, 0, 0);
566:             bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(PM_POWER_MODULE_NAME_CPU1, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
567: 
568: 			#if defined(RECV_CMD_LOG_FROM_MBOX)
569: 			void reset_forward_log_status(void);
570: 			// reset cpu1's log transfer status on cpu0.
571: 			reset_forward_log_status();
572: 			#endif
573: 
574:             start_cpu1_core();
575: 
576: 			previous_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
577: 			current_tick = previous_tick;
578: 			while((current_tick - previous_tick) < (PM_BOOT_CP1_WAITING_TIEM*AON_RTC_MS_TICK_CNT))
579: 			{
580: 				if (bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get()) // wait the cp1 response
581: 				{
582: 					break;
583: 				}
584: 				current_tick = bk_aon_rtc_get_current_tick(AON_RTC_ID_1);
585: 			}
586: 
587: 			if(!bk_pm_cp1_work_state_get())
588: 			{
589: 				os_printf("cp0 boot cp1[%d] time out, boot cp1 fail!!!\r\n",s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count);
590: 
591: 				/*Reset psram*/
592: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF);
593: 				bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MEDIA, PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON);
594: 
595: 				s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count++;
596: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count < PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
597: 				{
598: 					goto boot_cp1;
599: 				}
600: 				if(s_pm_cp1_boot_try_count == PM_BOOT_CP1_TRY_COUNT)
601: 				{
602: 					bk_wdt_force_reboot();//try 3 times, if fail ,reboot.
603: 				}
604: 			}
605: 		}
606: 	}
607: }

309: 		chip_id = s_psram_id.psram_id;
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	MEM_STATIC_LOGD("%s, chip_id:%x\r\n", __func__, chip_id);
313: 
314: 	actual_id = psram_hal_config_init(chip_id);
315: 	if (actual_id == 0) {
316: 		MEM_STATIC_LOGE("%s, fail!\r\n", __func__);
317: 		if (!is_skip_mutex) {
318: 			rtos_unlock_mutex(&s_psram_mutex);

321: 	}

323: 	bk_delay_us(1000);
324: 	psram_hal_set_default_clk();

106: static unsigned int channel_index(uint8_t logical_channel)
107: {
108:   unsigned int i;

110:   for (i = 0; i < sizeof(g_channel_ids); i++)
111:     {

121: static uint16_t uart_count(void)
122: {
123:   if (g_uart_write >= g_uart_read)
124:     {
125:       return g_uart_write - g_uart_read;
126:     }
127: 
128:   return UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart_read + g_uart_write;
129: }

131: static void uart_prepare(void)
132: {
133:   struct logical_channel *channel = &g_channels[2];
134:   uint16_t count;
135:   uint16_t first;
136: 
137:   if (channel->pending || g_uart_inflight != 0)
138:     {
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - g_uart_retry_after) < 0)
143:     {
144:       return;
145:     }
146: 
147:   count = uart_count();
148:   if (count == 0)
149:     {
150:       return;
151:     }
152: 
153:   if (count > UART_XCHG_SIZE)
154:     {
155:       count = UART_XCHG_SIZE;
156:     }
157: 
158:   first = UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart_read;
159:   if (first > count)
160:     {
161:       first = count;
162:     }
163: 
164:   memcpy(g_uart_xchg, &g_uart_tx[g_uart_read], first);
165:   if (first != count)
166:     {
167:       memcpy(&g_uart_xchg[first], g_uart_tx, count - first);
168:     }
169: 
170:   channel->message.header = 0; /* MB_UART_SEND_DATA */
171:   channel->message.param1 = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_uart_xchg;
172:   channel->message.param2 = count;
173:   channel->message.param3 = 0; /* RTS deasserted, CRC disabled by Armino. */
174:   channel->pending = true;
175:   g_uart_inflight = count;
176: }

178: static int dispatch_locked(void)
179: {
180:   struct logical_channel *channel;
181:   uint32_t wire[2];
182:   clock_t now;
183:   unsigned int i;
184:   int ret;
185: 
186:   now = clock_systime_ticks();
187:   if (g_phy_busy && now - g_busy_since >= PHY_BUSY_TIMEOUT)
188:     {
189:       g_stats.ack_timeout++;
190:       g_phy_busy = false;
191:     }
192: 
193:   if (g_phy_busy)
194:     {
195:       return OK;
196:     }
197: 
198:   if (g_ack_wire[0] != 0)
199:     {
200:       ret = bk7258_mbox_send(0, g_ack_wire);
201:       if (ret < 0)
202:         {
203:           if (ret == -EAGAIN)
204:             {
205:               g_stats.fifo_full++;
206:             }
207: 
208:           return ret;
209:         }
210: 
211:       g_ack_wire[0] = 0;
212:       g_stats.tx_count++;
213:     }
214: 
215:   uart_prepare();
216:   for (i = 0; i < sizeof(g_channel_ids); i++)
217:     {
218:       channel = &g_channels[i];
219:       if (!channel->pending)
220:         {
221:           continue;
222:         }
223: 
224:       g_active_channel = g_channel_ids[i];
225:       g_active_seq = ++g_tx_seq;
226:       channel->message.header &= 0xffu;
227:       channel->message.header |= (uint32_t)g_active_seq << 16;
228:       channel->message.header |= (uint32_t)g_active_channel << 24;
229:       wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&channel->message;
230:       wire[1] = sizeof(channel->message);
231:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
232:       ret = bk7258_mbox_send(0, wire);
233:       if (ret < 0)
234:         {
235:           if (ret == -EAGAIN)
236:             {
237:               g_stats.fifo_full++;
238:             }
239: 
240:           return ret;
241:         }
242: 
243:       g_phy_busy = true;
244:       g_busy_since = now;
245:       g_stats.tx_count++;
246:       return OK;
247:     }
248: 
249:   return OK;
250: }

257:   (void)argv;

259:     {

261: 
262:       flags = up_irq_save();
263:       if (g_serial_kick)
264:         {
265:           g_serial_kick = false;
266:           up_irq_restore(flags);
267:           bk7258_serial_tx_available();
268:           flags = up_irq_save();
269:         }
270: 
271:       (void)dispatch_locked();
272:       up_irq_restore(flags);
273:     }

278: static int queue_message(uint8_t logical_channel, uint8_t command,
279:                          uint32_t p1, uint32_t p2, uint32_t p3)
280: {
281:   struct logical_channel *channel;
282:   irqstate_t flags;
283:   unsigned int index;
284:   int ret;
285: 
286:   if (!g_initialized)
287:     {
288:       return -EAGAIN;
289:     }
290: 
291:   index = channel_index(logical_channel);
292:   if (index >= sizeof(g_channel_ids))
293:     {
294:       return -EINVAL;
295:     }
296: 
297:   flags = up_irq_save();
298:   channel = &g_channels[index];
299:   if (channel->pending)
300:     {
301:       up_irq_restore(flags);
302:       return -EBUSY;
303:     }
304: 
305:   channel->message.header = command;
306:   channel->message.param1 = p1;
307:   channel->message.param2 = p2;
308:   channel->message.param3 = p3;
309:   channel->pending = true;
310:   ret = dispatch_locked();
311:   up_irq_restore(flags);
312:   nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
313:   return ret == -EAGAIN ? OK : ret;
314: }

316: static bool valid_cp_message(const bk7258_mbox_message_t *wire,
317:                              uintptr_t *address)
318: {
319:   *address = wire->data[0];
320:   /* Armino's mbox0_adapter mailbox_buff is an array of 16-byte messages in
321:    * CP .bss and is only word-aligned; 32-byte alignment is reserved for the
322:    * separate exchange payload buffers. */
323:   return wire->src_cpu == 0 && wire->data[1] == sizeof(struct mb_message) &&
324:          (*address & 3u) == 0 && *address >= CP_RAM_START &&
325:          *address <= CP_RAM_END - sizeof(struct mb_message);
326: }
327: 
328: static void handle_ack(struct mb_message *message)
329: {
330:   uint8_t logical_channel = message->header >> 24;
331:   uint8_t sequence = message->header >> 16;
332:   bool uart_failed;
333:   unsigned int index;
334: 
335:   if ((message->header & ((uint32_t)CHNL_CTRL_RESET << 12)) != 0)
336:     {
337:       g_stats.reset_count++;
338:       g_phy_busy = false;
339:       (void)dispatch_locked();
340:       return;
341:     }
342: 
343:   if (logical_channel != g_active_channel || sequence != g_active_seq)
344:     {
345:       /* An ACK from a timed-out transmission may arrive after the same
346:        * logical channel has already been retried with a new sequence. It is
347:        * stale and must not release the current in-flight transaction. */
348:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
349:       return;
350:     }
351: 
352:   index = channel_index(g_active_channel);
353:   if (index >= sizeof(g_channel_ids) || !g_channels[index].pending)
354:     {
355:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
356:       g_phy_busy = false;
357:       (void)dispatch_locked();
358:       return;
359:     }
360: 
361:   g_channels[index].pending = false;
362:   if (g_active_channel == MB_CHNL_UART0_TX)
363:     {
364:       uart_failed =
365:         (message->header & ((uint32_t)CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL << 8)) != 0 ||
366:         (message->param1 & 2u) != 0;
367:       if (uart_failed)
368:         {
369:           g_stats.uart_tx_fail++;
370:           g_uart_inflight = 0;
371:           g_uart_retry_after = clock_systime_ticks() + TX_RETRY_INTERVAL;
372:         }
373:       else
374:         {
375:           g_uart_read = (g_uart_read + g_uart_inflight) % UART_TX_SIZE;
376:           g_uart_inflight = 0;
377:           g_uart_retry_after = 0;
378:           g_serial_kick = true;
379:         }
380: 
381:       nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
382:     }
383: 
384:   g_phy_busy = false;
385:   uart_prepare();
386:   (void)dispatch_locked();
387: }

389: static void mailbox_rx(const bk7258_mbox_message_t *wire)
390: {
391:   struct mb_message message;
392:   uintptr_t address;
393:   uint8_t control;
394:   uint8_t logical_channel;
395:   irqstate_t flags;
396: 
397:   if (!valid_cp_message(wire, &address))
398:     {
399:       g_stats.bad_envelope++;
400:       return;
401:     }
402: 
403:   memcpy(&message, (const void *)address, sizeof(message));
404:   control = (message.header >> 12) & 0x0fu;
405:   logical_channel = message.header >> 24;
406:   g_stats.rx_count++;
407: 
408:   flags = up_irq_save();
409:   if ((control & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0)
410:     {
411:       handle_ack(&message);
412:       up_irq_restore(flags);
413:       return;
414:     }
415: 
416:   if (logical_channel != MB_CHNL_PWC_RX &&
417:       logical_channel != MB_CHNL_UART0_RX)
418:     {
419:       g_stats.bad_envelope++;
420:       up_irq_restore(flags);
421:       return;
422:     }
423: 
424:   if (logical_channel == MB_CHNL_UART0_RX)
425:     {
426:       /* This port is output-only, but Armino initializes MB_UART0 by sending
427:        * SEND_STATE from CP. Acknowledge its state/data commands with RTS
428:        * deasserted so the CP endpoint reaches ready without enabling input. */
429:       if ((message.header & 0xffu) != MB_UART_SEND_DATA &&
430:           (message.header & 0xffu) != MB_UART_SEND_STATE)
431:         {
432:           message.header |= (uint32_t)CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL << 8;
433:         }
434: 
435:       message.param1 = 0; /* uart_rts=0, uart_tx_fail=0 */
436:       message.param2 = 0;
437:       message.param3 = 0;
438:     }
439: 
440:   if ((control & CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
441:     {
442:       message.header |= (uint32_t)CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX << 12;
443:       memcpy((void *)address, &message, sizeof(message));
444:       memcpy(&g_ack_message, &message, sizeof(g_ack_message));
445:       g_ack_wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&g_ack_message;
446:       g_ack_wire[1] = sizeof(g_ack_message);
447:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
448:       if (bk7258_mbox_send(0, g_ack_wire) < 0)
449:         {
450:           g_stats.fifo_full++;
451:           nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
452:         }
453:       else
454:         {
455:           g_ack_wire[0] = 0;
456:           g_stats.tx_count++;
457:         }
458: 
459:       message.header &= ~((uint32_t)CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX << 12);
460:     }
461: 
462:   if (logical_channel == MB_CHNL_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
463:     {
464:       g_pwc_rx(&message);
465:     }
466: 
467:   up_irq_restore(flags);
468: }

text:
## Scope and conclusion

The BK7258 AP/CP power-control protocol is carried on mailbox logical channel `MB_CHNL_PWC`. Its application payload is a fixed 16-byte message:

```c
header/mb_chnl_hdr_t
param1
param2
param3
```

Commands `0x7`, `0x8`, `0x9`, and `0xa` participate directly or indirectly in PSRAM ownership/lifetime management. Command `0xc` is a generic AP-to-CP PM-data query and does **not** expose PSRAM state, device ID, or capacity.

The most important compatibility findings are:

1. In current `bk_avdk_smp`, command `0x7` does **not** return `bk_err_t` in `param1`; CP returns the requested `pm_power_module_state_e` (`0` on, `1` off). This differs from older `bk_idk`.
2. Command `0x8` is overloaded:
   - `param1 == 0`: request AP allocator usage, followed by a command-`0x8` semantic response.
   - `param1 == 1`: asynchronous “PSRAM powered off” notification; no semantic response is expected.
3. Command `0x9` requests allocator diagnostics and has no semantic response.
4. Command `0xa` is the AP-recovery/shutdown callback mechanism, not a PSRAM-information query.
5. Command `0xc` only supports three PM data selectors: startup interval, deep-sleep wake source, and low-voltage wake source.
6. The CP PSRAM driver internally knows initialization state and detected ID, but current `bk_avdk_smp` does not export either through PWC, and does not expose public ID/capacity getters.
7. A detected/configured capacity mismatch is only logged as a warning. Initialization still succeeds, and the compile-time memory map is not clamped to actual capacity.

---

# 1. Wire format and mailbox synchronization

## 1.1 Exact wire data types

The AP mailbox definition is:

- `mb_chnl_hdr_t`: 32-bit union:
  - `cmd`: 8 bits
  - `state`: 4 bits
  - reserved: 20 bits
- `mb_chnl_cmd_t`:
  - `mb_chnl_hdr_t hdr`
  - `u32 param1`
  - `u32 param2`
  - `u32 param3`

See:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:109-127`
- CP-identical definition:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:108-126`

Thus the semantic message is exactly 16 bytes and consists only of four 32-bit words. There are no PSRAM-specific wire structs.

The mailbox callback types are:

```c
typedef void (*chnl_tx_cmpl_isr_t)(void *param, mb_chnl_ack_t *ack_buf);
typedef void (*chnl_tx_isr_t)(void *param);
typedef void (*chnl_rx_isr_t)(void *param, mb_chnl_cmd_t *cmd_buf);
```

References:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:136-156`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:135-155`

The PWC channel identifiers are established in the per-core logical-channel enums:

- AP/CPU1 → CP/CPU0: `MB_CHNL_PWC` at the third CPU1→CPU0 logical channel:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:75-99`
- CP/CPU0 → AP/CPU1:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:62-87`

## 1.2 Transport ACK versus semantic PM response

These are distinct:

1. The mailbox logical-channel layer supplies a transport-level acknowledgement.
2. PWC commands frequently generate a second PWC message with the same command number as the semantic response.

The mailbox API even defines `MB_CHNL_WRITE_SYNC`, but the PM code does not use it for these operations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:158-166`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:227-244`

Both AP and CP instead call `mb_chnl_write()` asynchronously and maintain their own completion state variables.

AP initialization registers all three callbacks, although TX and TX-completion callbacks are empty:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:285-288`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:445-454`

CP does the same:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:196-200`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:280-289`

## 1.3 Message-send retry behavior

Current SMP AP sends a PWC message through `pm_cp1_mailbox_send_data()`:

- fills `hdr.cmd`, `param1`, `param2`, `param3`;
- calls `mb_chnl_write(MB_CHNL_PWC, ...)`;
- retries after 2 ms;
- gives up after more than five retries.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:260-283`

CP uses essentially the same retry loop, with an additional mailbox sleep vote around the send:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:164-189`

The CP mailbox status can be queried with `MB_CHNL_GET_STATUS`; `PM_CHNL_STATE_BUSY == 1`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:50-51`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:760-765`

## 1.4 ISR-to-thread handoff

In current SMP, the CP RX ISR does not perform PSRAM initialization directly. For command `0x7`, it creates a `low_pwr_core_msg_t` and pushes it to the low-power worker queue:

- RX dispatch:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:200-225`
- Internal type:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/low_pwr_core.h:4-29`
- Queue push:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/low_pwr_core.c:135-158`
- Worker receive and dispatch:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/low_pwr_core.c:159-170`

This is the correct model for OpenVela as well: copy/enqueue in mailbox context, perform PM callbacks and allocator operations in a worker thread.

---

# 2. Command constants and associated enums

The exact command constants are:

```c
#define PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD              0x7
#define PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD        0x8
#define PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD    0x9
#define PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD                  0xa
#define PM_GET_PM_DATA_CMD                   0xc
```

References:

- CP: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:25-40`
- AP: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:26-41`

## PSRAM vote module enum

`pm_power_psram_module_name_e` is the command-`0x7` `param1` type. Current CP values are:

| Value | Enumerator |
|---:|---|
| 0 | `PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_FFT` |
| 1 | `...AUDP_SBC` |
| 2 | `...AUDP_AUDIO` |
| 3 | `...AUDP_I2S` |
| 4 | `...VIDP_JPEG_EN` |
| 5 | `...VIDP_H264_EN` |
| 6 | `...VIDP_JPEG_DE` |
| 7 | `...VIDP_DMA2D` |
| 8 | `...VIDP_LCD` |
| 9 | `...APP` |
| 10 | `...AS_MEM` |
| 11 | `...CPU1` |
| 12 | `...MEDIA` |
| 13 | `...LVGL_CODE_RUN` |
| 14 | `...AS_SECTIONS` |
| 15 | `...FORCE_ON` — CP header only |
| 16 | `...MAX` — CP header |

References:

- CP enum:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:129-148`
- AP enum, which ends at `AS_SECTIONS` and then `MAX`:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:134-152`

This AP/CP header asymmetry matters. OpenVela should not assume AP’s `MAX` value is a valid CP vote module, and should use an explicitly supported module value rather than serializing a local `MAX`.

## Power-state enum

Command-`0x7` `param2` and current SMP response `param1` use:

```c
typedef enum
{
    PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON = 0,
    PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF,
    PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_NONE
} pm_power_module_state_e;
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/modules/pm.h:238-243`

Therefore:

- `0` means **on**
- `1` means **off**
- `2` means **none/invalid**

This is easy to misread because “success” is also conventionally zero.

---

# 3. Command `0x7`: PSRAM power vote/control

## 3.1 AP → CP request

Current SMP AP sends:

```text
cmd    = 0x7
param1 = pm_power_psram_module_name_e module
param2 = pm_power_module_state_e power_state
param3 = 0
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:457-470`

The public API is:

```c
bk_err_t bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(
    pm_power_psram_module_name_e module,
    pm_power_module_state_e power_state);
```

Documented at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:552-568`

## 3.2 CP handling

The CP RX ISR maps the request to:

```text
LOW_PWR_CORE_PSRAM_POWER
param1 = module
param2 = power_state
param3 = original param3
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:223-225`

The worker calls:

```c
bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl(msg.param1, msg.param2);
```

then sends:

```text
cmd    = 0x7
param1 = msg.param2       // requested ON/OFF state
param2 = 0
param3 = 0
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/low_pwr_core.c:216-220`

Notably, `ret` from `bk_pm_module_vote_psram_ctrl()` is computed but **not returned**. Thus current SMP command `0x7` response conveys the resulting/requested state, not an error code.

## 3.3 CP vote bitmap and physical transition

CP maintains:

```c
static uint32_t s_pm_psram_ctrl_state;
```

Each module corresponds to a bit. On an ON vote:

- raise VDDDIG if this is the first vote;
- call `bk_psram_init()`;
- retry initialization up to three calls total;
- optionally watchdog-reboot after the third failure;
- set the module bit.

On OFF:

- clear the module bit;
- only physically deinitialize when the bitmap becomes zero and PSRAM is not force-on;
- lower VDDDIG;
- set the shared power-down magic;
- notify/query AP using command `0x8` with `param1 == 1`.

References:

- bitmap and implementation:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:627-687`
- public wrapper:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:704-719`
- magic value and shared fields:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:46-94`

The CP sets the vote bit even if initialization failed and watchdog support is disabled, because bit-setting occurs after the retry block regardless of final `ret`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:643-665`

That is another reason OpenVela should not infer “hardware definitely initialized” solely from receiving state `ON`.

## 3.4 AP response handling and callbacks

AP command-`0x7` RX handling:

- `param1 == 0` (`PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON`):
  - queue `PM_AP_CORE_PSRAM_STATE_NOTIFY`
  - set message state to `PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_ON`
- `param1 == 1`:
  - no callback is queued in this branch
- any other value:
  - local `ret = BK_FAIL`
- in all cases, set the command-`0x7` completion state to `FINISH`.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:346-363`

The synchronous AP caller:

- clears `s_pm_psram_power_ctrl` to `INIT`;
- sends command `0x7`;
- busy-waits against the AP AON counter for nominally 100 ms;
- logs timeout;
- nevertheless returns `BK_OK`;
- for ON, invokes the PSRAM callback directly after the wait.

Reference:

- completion state:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:237-245`
- send/wait:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:457-496`

The direct callback at lines 488-491 means the separately queued ON notification from RX can be redundant; the worker’s ON branch is currently empty:

- queued message:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:346-353`
- worker:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_core.c:103-119`

## 3.5 Difference from older `bk_idk`

Older IDK CP treats command `0x7` as a direct RPC and replies with `bk_err_t`:


# 4. Command `0x8`: allocator state query and power-off notification

Command `0x8` is bidirectional and overloaded.

## 4.1 CP → AP allocator usage query

Current SMP CP calls:

```c
bk_pm_get_cp1_psram_malloc_count(uint32_t using_psram_type);
```

Reference:

- declaration:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/pwr_clk.h:399-413`
- implementation:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:521-556`

For `using_psram_type == 0`, it sends:

```text
cmd    = 0x8
param1 = 0
param2 = 0
param3 = 0
```

Then it:

- clears `s_pm_cp1_psram_malloc_state`;
- clears cached count;
- waits up to 100 ms using CP AON RTC;
- returns `s_pm_cp1_psram_malloc_count`;
- returns zero immediately if AP/CPU1 is not boot-ready.

References:

- state variables:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:62-65`
- state accessors:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:132-149`
- request and wait:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:522-555`

## 4.2 AP handling of query

When AP receives command `0x8`, `param1 == 0`, it queues:

```text
event  = PM_AP_CORE_PSRAM_STATE_NOTIFY
param1 = PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD  // numeric 8
param2 = incoming param2
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:364-382`

The AP worker obtains:

```c
uint32_t used_count = bk_psram_heap_get_used_count();
```

and sends the semantic response:

```text
cmd    = 0x8
param1 = 0x8             // response discriminator, not a status
param2 = used_count
param3 = 0
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_core.c:114-118`

The CP receives that response and recognizes it only if:

```c
cmd_buf->param1 == PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD
```

It then stores `param2` and marks the wait complete:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:234-240`

Thus `param2` is specifically the AP allocator’s used-byte/count value returned by `bk_psram_heap_get_used_count()`. It is not device capacity.

## 4.3 CP → AP power-off notification

When the CP vote bitmap reaches zero, it does:

```c
bk_pm_get_cp1_psram_malloc_count(0x1);
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:674-681`

For nonzero `using_psram_type`, the function sends command `0x8` but does not wait:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:526-550`

The resulting message is:

```text
cmd    = 0x8
param1 = 1   // PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_OFF
param2 = 0
param3 = 0
```

AP recognizes `param1 == PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_OFF`, queues a PSRAM-off callback message, and does not send a command-`0x8` semantic response:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:364-371`

The worker then invokes all registered PSRAM-off callbacks:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_core.c:103-109`
- callback dispatch:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_misc.c:326-353`

This notification occurs **after** CP has called `bk_psram_deinit()`, so it is not a pre-power-down veto or prepare handshake:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:675-680`

## 4.4 Older-IDK discriminator difference

Older IDK used:

- request: `param1 = 0`
- response: `param1 = 1`
- `param2 = used_count`

References:

- request:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:716-742`
- AP response:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:339-342`
- CP recognition:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pwr_clk.c:477-483`

Current SMP instead uses response discriminator `param1 = 0x8`, reserving `1` as the PSRAM-off notification. OpenVela must use the SMP form.

# 8. PSRAM callbacks and AP-local callback data types

PSRAM callback types are AP-local; they are not sent over the mailbox.

```c
typedef enum
{
    PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_ON = 0,
    PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_OFF,
    PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_MAX
} pm_ap_psram_power_state_e;

typedef bk_err_t (*psram_power_state_callback_fn)(
    uint32_t param1, uint32_t param2);

typedef struct
{
    pm_power_psram_module_name_e dev_id;
    psram_power_state_callback_fn psram_on_cb_fn;
    psram_power_state_callback_fn psram_off_cb_fn;
    uint32_t param1;
    uint32_t param2;
} pm_ap_psram_power_state_callback_info_t;
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/pm_ap_core.h:46-72`

Registration stores callbacks indexed by `dev_id` and initializes callback-state bitmaps:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_misc.c:280-298`

Dispatch behavior:

- ON callback is executed only for bits in `s_pm_handle_psram_callback_state`, then its bit is cleared.
- OFF invokes all registered OFF callbacks and re-arms all corresponding ON bits.
- Stored `param1` and `param2` are currently ignored during dispatch; callbacks are invoked as `callback(0, 0)`.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/driver/pwr_clk/pm_ap_misc.c:326-353`

This means OpenVela does not need to emulate the callback registry to be wire-compatible. It only needs an internal mechanism to wake any PSRAM users and quiesce them on notification.

where:

# 10. Device IDs and initialization behavior

The recognized IDs are:

```c
PSRAM_APS6408L_ID       = 0x8d09  // 8 MiB
PSRAM_APS128XXO_OB9_ID  = 0x8d08  // 16 MiB
PSRAM_W955D8MKY_5J_ID   = 0x1c8f or 0x1f8f by configuration // treated as 4 MiB
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/include/psram_hal.h:39-46`

The current CP initialization sequence is:

1. Return immediately if already initialized.
2. Reject interrupt-context initialization.
3. Lazily create and lock a PSRAM mutex.
4. Select 1.95 V.
5. Enable PSRAM power and clock.
6. Use cached flash ID if valid, otherwise probe.
7. Call `psram_hal_config_init()`.
8. Fail only if returned `actual_id == 0`.
9. Set default clock.
10. Warn on capacity mismatch.
11. update cached ID;
12. set `s_psram_init_done = true`.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c:249-369`

PSRAM is also explicitly initialized at CP driver startup in this tree:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/common/driver.c:553-563`

Therefore AP startup may find the PHY already active before sending its first command-`0x7` vote. A vote is still needed to prevent later CP vote-based shutdown.

# 11. Capacity mismatch behavior and hazards

Current SMP defines:

```c
PSRAM_4M_SIZE  = 0x00400000
PSRAM_8M_SIZE  = 0x00800000
PSRAM_16M_SIZE = 0x01000000
```

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c:32-34`

After successful hardware initialization, the driver compares detected ID against `CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY`:

- W955 → expect 4 MiB;
- APS6408L → expect 8 MiB;
- APS128 → expect 16 MiB;
- unknown → warning.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c:328-344`

## Exact mismatch result

A mismatch:

- only logs `MEM_STATIC_LOGW`;
- does not return an error;
- does not change `CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY`;
- does not clamp heap or MPU regions;
- does not alter detected ID;
- continues to set `s_psram_init_done = true`;
- returns `BK_OK`.

References:

- warning:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c:328-344`
- successful completion:
  `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/psram/psram_driver.c:346-369`

Thus a 4/8 MiB physical device with a 16 MiB link/layout remains a successful initialization from the driver’s perspective. High addresses can alias or corrupt lower physical PSRAM.

## Probe caveats

The HAL probe order is:

1. 8 MiB APS6408L;
2. 16 MiB APS128;
3. W955.

Reference:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/psram_hal.c:362-413`

There are two weak behaviors:

1. When a nonzero cached ID is supplied, `psram_hal_config_init()` ignores the specific initializer’s failure return and returns the cached `type` anyway:
   `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/psram_hal.c:375-391`
2. The final W955 branch returns `type` without testing its `ret`:
   `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/common/hal/psram_hal.c:409-413`

So `actual_id != 0` is not a strong guarantee that the selected ID was positively verified in every path.

# 13. Smallest protocol-compatible OpenVela design

The minimal implementation should preserve the exact four-word protocol and add no CP-defined fields.

## 13.1 Define only the existing command and enum values

Locally define:

```c
#define PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD           0x7u
#define PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD     0x8u
#define PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD 0x9u
#define PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD               0xau
#define PM_GET_PM_DATA_CMD                0xcu

#define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON          0u
#define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF         1u

#define PM_AP_PSRAM_POWER_OFF             1u
```

Use explicit `uint32_t` fields on wire. Do not depend on C enum size across OpenVela/Armino builds.

## 13.2 Keep PSRAM physically on while OpenVela maps or executes from it

The current OpenVela layout reserves AP PSRAM sections at `0x60a00000..0x61000000`:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_psram.h:22-27`

If any live AP code, data, heap, or slab relies on this mapping, OpenVela should send one command-`0x7` ON vote at PWC startup and retain it for the entire AP lifetime:

```text
cmd    = 0x7
param1 = a real supported module, preferably AS_SECTIONS (14)
param2 = ON (0)
param3 = 0
```

Do not send OFF while OpenVela still has mapped/live PSRAM users.

Do not serialize AP’s `PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_NAME_MAX`; AP and CP disagree about where `MAX` falls. Use the explicit supported numeric module.

If the CP configuration accepts and intentionally uses `FORCE_ON` value 15, that is CP-defined, but AP’s current public enum does not contain it. The least surprising protocol-compatible choice is therefore the AP-defined `AS_SECTIONS` vote, value 14.

## 13.3 Handle incoming `0x7` as a state response only

Record:

- `param1 == 0`: CP reports ON;
- `param1 == 1`: CP reports OFF;
- otherwise protocol/error state.

Wake a waiter if OpenVela’s startup sends an ON vote. Do not interpret `param2` as ID or capacity; current CP sends it as zero.

Because CP’s current implementation does not return the initialization `ret`, receiving ON is not an absolute hardware-probe guarantee. Treat it as vote/protocol completion, then rely on a controlled memory smoke test only if the product requires one.

## 13.4 Implement command `0x8` exactly

For incoming:

```text
cmd=0x8, param1=0
```

obtain the real amount used by the OpenVela PSRAM allocator, if one exists, and reply:

```text
cmd    = 0x8
param1 = 0x8
param2 = actual_used_count
param3 = 0
```

If OpenVela has no dynamic allocator in PSRAM and only fixed statically reserved regions, returning zero for **allocator usage** is compatible, provided it means “no dynamic PSRAM allocations.” It must not be presented as “PSRAM unused” if fixed code/data/slabs remain live.

For incoming:

```text
cmd=0x8, param1=1
```

mark PSRAM unavailable and invoke local off/quiesce notification. Send no semantic command-`0x8` response.

Ideally this notification should never occur while the retained `AS_SECTIONS` ON vote exists. If it does occur, treat it as a fatal lifecycle inconsistency rather than probing or accessing PSRAM.

## 13.5 Implement `0x9` as diagnostics only

Dump actual allocator/fixed-region accounting if available. Otherwise no-op after transport ACK. Send no response.

## 13.6 Implement only necessary `0xa` recovery behavior

On incoming command `0xa`:

1. quiesce OpenVela services;
2. stop users of shared PSRAM/mailbox resources;
3. only send module `INIT`/`FINISH` responses for module IDs OpenVela genuinely implements.

Wire form:

```text
cmd    = 0xa
param1 = supported recovery module ID
param2 = 0 or 1
param3 = 0
```

Do not invent a “PSRAM complete,” “capacity,” or “device ID” recovery module. The supplied vendor tree does not define one.

If the platform does not yet support AP shutdown, retaining the AP/PSRAM vote and explicitly declining to claim recovery completion is safer than sending fabricated completion states.

## 13.7 Do not extend `0xc`

If OpenVela needs the existing PM queries, support only selector values `0`, `1`, and `2`, with response data taken from `param2`.

Do **not** define unofficial selectors for:

- initialized state;
- PSRAM ID;
- capacity.

The CP has no matching implementation. Such requests would fall through to the CP default selector path and return zero, which is ambiguous and unsafe.

## 13.8 Capacity policy

Because CP does not report capacity over PWC, the smallest safe product implementation is:

1. keep the validated 16 MiB OpenVela static layout only for boards whose fitted PSRAM part is known to be 16 MiB;
2. retain the compile-time 16 MiB consistency check;
3. fail board qualification/build configuration if hardware BOM and CP `CONFIG_PSRAM_CAPACITY` disagree;
4. do not treat CP command-`0x7` ON as proof of 16 MiB;
5. do not add capacity to an existing response field.

If runtime capacity discovery is mandatory, it requires either:

- an explicit versioned CP protocol extension implemented on both sides; or
- an early destructive alias probe before any AP/CP PSRAM allocation or code placement.

The former is cleaner but is outside the existing protocol. The latter is not a minimal PWC implementation and is unsafe once shared PSRAM is live.

# Final recommendation

The smallest faithful OpenVela implementation is:

- leave the existing 16-byte mailbox transport unchanged;
- add a tiny PWC semantic state machine in `bk7258_pm_pwc.c`;
- send and retain one command-`0x7` `AS_SECTIONS` ON vote;
- wait for the current-SMP state-valued `0x7` response;
- answer only command-`0x8,param1=0` with `{0x8, 0x8, real_dynamic_used_count, 0}`;
- treat `0x8,param1=1` as an off notification;
- make `0x9` diagnostic-only;
- use `0xa` solely for genuine shutdown callbacks;
- keep `0xc` limited to its three existing PM selectors;
- expose no fabricated CP PSRAM initialized/ID/capacity values.

That is protocol-compatible with the supplied `bk_avdk_smp` CP and avoids mistakenly importing older `bk_idk` response semantics or local-only PSRAM getter APIs into the wire protocol.
